text:
marta: Heads-up — we're seeing a spike in tiny-GPU pod evictions in ap-southeast1 since ~08:10 UTC. Many show AttachTimeout / Attach failed then preempted. Fragmentation is getting worse, scheduling can't pack.
infra-bot: ALERT: GPU_POD_ATTACH_ERRORS ap-southeast1 x9 in last 5m. Top errors: AttachVolume timeout, CSI attach delayed.
josh: Any events/logs for one of the failing pods? paste `kubectl describe` output please.
marta: Paste of event from one evicted pod:
```
Events:
  Normal  Scheduled  3m   default-scheduler  Successfully assigned team-a/model-train-1 to node-ap-1
  Warning FailedAttachVolume  2m   attach-detacher  AttachVolume.Attach failed for volume "pvc-123" : rpc timeout after 30s
  Warning  Failed  1m   kubelet  Evicted: Preemption due to higher priority pod
```
kai: That looks like CSI attach latency + then preemption/anti-affinity forcing scatter. If attach takes 30s+ we lose packing windows and scheduler spreads pods to other AZs.
ashley: Do we have a PromQL to show attach latency and attach error rate so we can correlate with network/egress saturation?
josh: Try this quick one: `sum(rate(csi_plugin_attach_duration_seconds_count{region="ap-southeast1"}[5m])) by (status)` and `histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(csi_plugin_attach_duration_seconds_bucket{region="ap-southeast1"}[5m])) by (le))`
marta: Ran the histogram — p99 attach is ~120s for the past 10m, errors spiking. Egress bandwidth on host pool shows bursts at same time.
sre-oncall: Immediate mitigations I can do: 1) bump warm pool for ap-southeast1 from 10 -> 14 nodes for 30m, 2) temporarily relax the inter-pod anti-affinity rule for tiny gpu pods (label: workload=small-gpu) to allow co-locating 2 per node, 3) add a short grace to the preemption window to avoid immediate eviction during attach. Thoughts?
kai: Agree. Also roll a restart of the CSI driver on a canary subset — sometimes long-lived CSI connections cause attach stalls. If CSI restart reduces p99 quickly we know it's driver-related.
ashley: Command to relax anti-affinity (example):
```bash
kubectl patch poddisruptionbudget -n teams --type=json --patch='[ {"op":"replace","path":"/spec/selector/matchLabels/affinityLocked","value":"false"} ]'
# or patch the Deployment pod template to remove requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution -> preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution for a short window
```
We'll prepare a controlled patch and rollout to a canary namespace first.
josh: I'll also add a short scheduler scoring tweak in the canary to bias for packing tiny-gpu pods to nodes with available PCI affinity (~+10 score) so we can test fewer AZ hops.
marta: After bumping warm pool and relaxing affinity, we saw evictions drop by ~60% in first 10m. CSI restarts on 3 nodes cleared stuck attaches on those nodes.
sre-oncall: Done: warm pool bumped, affinity relaxation applied to canary, CSI driver restarted on canary nodes. Monitoring continues. Keeping autoscaler manual for now.
kai: Long term: propose two things — increase CSI attach timeout to 120s in our kubelet/driver config and add a scheduling plugin that prefers gang packing for tiny GPU pods (allowing 2/3 to share node if >0.5 GPU each). I'll write RFC.
ashley: I opened infra RFC: 1743000011 describing attach-timeout change and packing plugin + rollout plan. Linking later.
infra-bot: NOTE: Incident ticket #INC-2024-823 created for ap-southeast1 attach surge.
marta: Quick action notes for postmortem: - root cause likely intermittent egress saturation + CSI driver needing restart; - symptom amplification via strict anti-affinity and short preempt window; - mitigations applied: warm-pool bump, affinity relax, CSI restarts, scheduler bias canary. We'll keep warm pool elevated for 2h and revert affinity change after verification.
josh: Next steps: track p99 attach -> target <30s, monitor packing density metric, follow-up RFC for scheduler/batching heuristic.
sre-oncall: I'll file runbook steps to automate CSI rolling restart and add a prometheus alert for p99 attach >45s.
marta: Thanks all — will update on the incident channel and schedule postmortem meeting tomorrow 09:00 UTC. :thumbsup:
